# AGENTS.md

This file guides agents **contributing to this repository**. If you are an agent looking to *use* SingularityAPI from your own tool instead, read [INTEGRATING.md](INTEGRATING.md) — the agent-agnostic integration guide.

## DO NOT EDIT — Auto-generated Files

The following files are **idempotent** and regenerated by `scripts/update-models.js`. Never edit them directly — your changes will be overwritten on the next model sync.

| File | Why it's auto-generated |
|------|------------------------|
| `models.json` | Built from the SingularityAPI `/v1/models` response. `update-models.js` fetches models, preserves curated data for known IDs, and writes this file. |
| `deprecated-models.json` | Graveyard for models the API delisted. update-models.js stamps them with deprecatedAt and pi keeps serving them for a 2-week grace period, then evicts them. Never edit by hand. |
| `README.md` (model table) | The table under `## Available Models` is replaced in-place by `update-models.js` after merging base models → patch → custom models. |

## Correct Files to Edit

When a model needs overrides, new properties, or corrections, edit the appropriate source file below. These are the **source of truth** that the update script reads but never writes.

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `patch.json` | Per-model overrides keyed by model ID. Add reasoning flags, compat settings, pricing corrections, thinking level maps, etc. Applied on top of `models.json` at runtime and for README generation. |
| `custom-models.json` | Models that don't exist in the provider API (hidden models, contract slugs, cross-provider aliases). Merged after patch. Format: array of full model objects (same schema as `models.json` entries). |
| `index.ts` | Provider extension code. |
| `scripts/update-models.js` | The sync script itself (edit only if changing how models are fetched/transformed). |

## Data Flow

```
GET /v1/models  ──fetch──►  models.json  ──apply──►  patch.json  ──merge──►  custom-models.json
   (live caps +             (curated                (overrides)             (extra models)
    pricing, no-store)       metadata)                       │                      │
                                    └────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘
                                                         │
                                                 README model table
```

The runtime does the same merge in-memory on every session start (stale-while-revalidate): disk cache → embedded models.json first, then live `/v1/models` merged with embedded curation and hot-swapped in.

## Common Tasks

### Add a compat setting or override pricing for an existing model
→ Edit `patch.json`. Add an entry keyed by the model's `id`.

Note: `patch.json` carries the **reasoning entries for all reasoning-capable non-GPT-5.6 models**, verified against the gateway on 2026-09-13 (two probes, ~50 requests): DeepSeek V3.2/V4 family, Kimi K2.6/K2.7, and GLM 5.3 think at low/medium/high (xhigh/max 400, hidden); **Kimi K3 and GPT-6 Astra think at all five levels** (xhigh/max exposed). All maps omit `off` so thinking-off sends no `reasoning_effort` — for GPT-6 Astra this is mandatory (`"none"` 400s even on plain chat; opposite of the GPT-5.6 rule). `deepseek-v4.1-flash` accepts all levels but never thinks → kept non-reasoning (name-only patch). Quirks: `deepseek-v3.2`@low and `gpt-6-astra` below high may not think on trivial prompts. Once `/v1/models` advertises reasoning for a model, delete its patch entry and let the dynamic population take over.

### Add a model not listed by the provider API
→ Edit `custom-models.json`. Add a full model object to the array.

### Update models from the provider API
→ Run `node scripts/update-models.js` (requires `SINGULARITY_API_KEY` or a `singularity` credential in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`).

### Regenerate the README model table
→ Run `node scripts/update-models.js` — it updates both `models.json` and the README table.

### Cut a release (publish to npm)
CI publishes via **npm trusted publishing (OIDC)** — `.github/workflows/publish.yml`. No `NPM_TOKEN` secret.

- Merge a `model-sync` PR → patch bump (if `package.json` version is already on npm) then `npm publish`.
- **Actions → Publish → Run workflow** for code/docs releases (`patch` / `minor` / `major` / `skip`).

One-time npmjs.com setup (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher): GitHub Actions, user `WyrdWerk`, repo `pi-singularity-provider`, workflow filename `publish.yml`. New publishers default to stage-only — also allow **`npm publish`**. Direct-publish granular tokens (bypass-2FA) are being removed in January 2027; do not add one unless OIDC is unavailable.

Manual fallback: `bun test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` green, bump `version` in `package.json`, commit, `npm publish`. The README in the npm listing renders from the published tarball, so catalog/doc changes need a release to show up on npm.

## Provider Notes

- Base URL `https://api.singularityapi.dev/v1`, OpenAI-compatible (`openai-completions` API in pi).
- `GET /v1/models` requires auth and returns per-endpoint `capabilities` (context window, max/default output, 12-decimal pricing strings) — live data is authoritative for cost/contextWindow/maxTokens.
- Reasoning is **dynamic**: when `/v1/models` advertises it, the API wins over embedded curation (including an explicit "not supported"); while silent, curation stands. Recognized shapes on the chat-completions capability (then the model entry): `"reasoning": {"supported": bool, "efforts": [...]}` (canonical), bare `"reasoning": bool`, `reasoning_effort_values`/`reasoning_levels`/`thinking_levels` arrays, or `supported_parameters` containing `reasoning_effort`. `efforts` map onto pi levels (off→none, minimal→low fallback, others same-named); no levels given → default set none/low/medium/high.
- Display names are **not** exposed by the API — those are curated here.
- Models without a `/v1/chat/completions` capability (e.g. image-generation models) are skipped — never registered as chat models.
- Unsupported request parameters are rejected with a 400 (not ignored), so compat flags stay conservative: `supportsStore: false`, `supportsDeveloperRole: false`.
- GPT-5.6 models need an explicit `reasoning_effort` on tool calls; the extension maps every thinking level (off→"none") so it is always sent.
- Receipts: every response carries `x-singularity-receipt-id`; `GET /v1/receipts/{id}` resolves exact tokens/cost/latency (`/singularity-receipt` command).

## TL;DR

- **Never edit `models.json`** — edit `patch.json` instead.
- **Never edit the README model table** — run the update script instead.
- `patch.json` and `custom-models.json` are the source files you should modify.
